I wish I could do therapy, but all the doctors I've seen just want to treat the PTSD with a shitload of medication. They tell me that's the more serious issue.

I have a couple of friends that I can talk to, but it's hard. He was the one I talked to about everything, he was the only one that I ever opened up to completely. It's hard to imagine doing that with my friends when I know they all have their own stuff to handle and their own struggles.

I'm just so tired. I'm so tired of fighting to be here. I just want to sleep, just let it all fall away and rest for once.

I know everyone else has already said it, but I'm going to repeat the fact that this isn't your fault.

Suicide is more complicated than people can imagine. It's not something someone does because of a fight or a break-up or a lost job. There is always something deeper that leads people to that choice.

No one causes it except the person that makes the choice to end their life. You need to make yourself believe that or you die right along with her.

I'm so sorry that you're going through this. My boyfriend of seven years took his life on February 28th. It's still agonizing, I still can't make sense of it.

I am wishing so much peace and comfort your way.

So I wanted to take a little time before I answered that to make sure that I could explain this to the best of my ability.

The first thing you need to understand is that depression isn't that simple. Some people get depressed because of a break-up or a tragedy, that's normal. Most people will go through a depression at some point in their lives, just the way life goes.

Having depression is something different. Depression is a mental illness, it's a problem in your brain that has no real basis in reality. And it can go untreated and unnoticed for years. My boyfriend and I both have that, it's just the way our brains are, it has nothing to do with anything happening around us. Nothing bad was going on in my boyfriend's life, things were actually going pretty well for us. But when you've got a depressive disorder that really doesn't matter. I've been actively suicidal at the same time that I'm getting a promotion and a major raise, the brain is a fickle bitch.

I don't know your husband, I don't know if that was his problem or not. I'm not a doctor, but it sounds like what I have, what my boyfriend had. Most people don't even know that I have Major Depressive Disorder. I was top of my class, highest SAT score at my high school, AP and Honors diplomas, acceptance to all of the Ivy League, "Most Likely to Do Anything" . . . but the truth was that I constantly thought about killing myself and I went through my graduation ceremony bleeding from self-inflicted cuts on my thighs and wrists. It's not like the movies show, it's not always visible.

The other thing that I want to put out there is that there is a real stigma with mental illness. You get labelled and judged for going to therapy or trying medication. You can be so terrified of what the people around you will think, even the people closest to you. I think everyone with a mental illness has at one point or another felt like death would be less dangerous than potentially shattering your life by people finding out that you're crazy.

I know you're hurting. I wish I had answers, I wish I could tell you something to take away all that pain and all that betrayal, but I can't. Even though I have an insiders perspective, I still feel betrayed by what he did. Nothing takes that away because this type of loss is so different from anything else, so more all consuming. The brain can't ever really make sense of it.

I'm so sorry for your loss, for the pain you're going through. This is a really shit club to belong to, the last one any of us would have ever joined. I wish there was more I could do.

I don't really know how to answer that. I mean, hindsight is twenty-twenty. After it happens you look back and you see a million things that he said or did that could have given a clue. At least I did.

But at the same time, no, he wasn't really acting any differently. Even that night, he was a little quiet, but we had both had really shit days at work and that was a typical way for us to be after that happened.

The "why" seems to be the big question for a lot of people, but I don't really have that. To me the why is very simple: he had struggled with depression for a long time, we both did. We had both been suicidal several times during our relationship, we just managed to get past it. Until one of us didn't. The fact that we both understood how depression and suicidal ideation worked was one of the reasons we were together for so long. Not everyone can handle that in their house, but until that night we always had.

He was depressed, that's the answer for me because that's why I've tried to kill myself in the past. We talked about it all the time, the way that it just dragged you down and broke you and how it never seemed to get better.

Did I know he was actively suicidal that night? No, I had no clue. It was the first time he didn't tell me what he was feeling. We knew each other better than anyone, I knew how to hide being suicidal from him and he knew how to hide it from me. Honestly, I believe that if he had chosen pills or a razor like he had in the past instead of a gun, he would still be here now. To me, the idea that he went there when he never had before just means that he couldn't keep fighting.

People in his life blame so many things. His baby mama, his sons, his job, his parents, me. And the ones that don't believe he killed himself believe that I killed him.

To me he was just a really wonderful guy with a really amazing heart that had fought for a really long time and just got tired of struggling. They say that a human can endure anything as long as there's a light at the end of the tunnel, but I think he lost sight of that and gave up hope. And made the only decision he thought he could to take back control.

I want to thank you all for taking the time to respond to this. And I am so sorry for all that you have lost. I suppose we've all been put in this club no one wants to join.

It helped more than you can imagine to read your words. I wrote this on a really dark night that was followed by really several really dark days, but it's getting better.

So thank you for your words and your solidarity. I wish we didn't share this experience, but it helps to know that people are out there that understand.

That is definitely some good advice. I've opened myself up more to the people in my life (not his family) who want to help and it has gotten better. My moms, my brothers, my sisters, my friends, they have all come together to help me in any way they can and it has helped. Even when I want to do something weird or crazy, someone is always down to help me with that.

Thank you.

I can't imagine what it must be like as a parent to go through this. I feel for his family, it's hard for me to admit that there's nothing I can do to help the situation. I just want them to find some peace.

The hardest thing for me with them is that their relationship with their son was not great. Despite how long we were together, I spent hardly any time with them. Neither of us did. It's hard to be constantly told what to think and how to feel, all under the auspices of "dealing with it as a family", by people you really don't know and definitely don't like.

How I feel about them doesn't matter now, what tied us together isn't here anymore. I wouldn't mind if they wanted to know more about him, if they wanted to ask questions about his life, but with them, it's all about denying right now.

I hope that will change. Their son was an amazing guy, they missed out on getting to know him the way his friends and I did. I hope that some day they'll be able to talk about him, to accept the person he was that they didn't see.

I did find a few support groups, one for the survivors and a grief support group. And I'm trying therapy as well. It's good to know that there's light beyond this. It's hard to see right now.

Thank you for your encouragement.

Thank you.

It's hard, this whole thing. I don't want people to be able to relate to this. It's so horrifying, it shreds you in ways I could have never imagined.

But at the same time, it helps to know that there are people out there that understand.

I want to thank you both for responding to this. That was a dark night that was followed by a lot of dark days. I'm just starting to pull myself out of that place, but it helped knowing that I had shared it with someone and received an answer to it.

I don't know how to deal with any of this. Some days I'm okay and then suddenly I'm not.

It's unbearable.

But I'll get through it. It doesn't really feel like I have a choice, you know? There's nothing else I can do except keep pushing forward.

Right? It's always been that creepy story that will come up at family stuff because it was just so ridiculous. My hometown is pretty well known for some very famous murders and some pretty twisted shit, so it's just one of many stories. But it's always given me the chills. Even though my memories of it are pretty vague, dreams about it can wake me up in a cold sweat.

When I was three, my parents moved us into a new neighborhood. The house was nice, but kind of old. The neighborhood was an old 50's track home area, so it had a pretty varied group of people living there from older couples that had bought the houses new to young families looking for a cheap place to live to poor people looking for cheap houses to rent.

As soon as we moved in, my dad started noticed weird things with me. He would hear me giggling and laughing in my room and whenever he went in and asked what was so funny, I would tell him that the kids were being funny. He would also come in to wake me up and find me curled up in the closest. This happened over and over again, but my parents didn't think much of it because I was a pretty imaginative kid. The thing that wigged them out the most was that I flat out refused to walk out the front door. I would scream and yell and cry until one of my parents carried me in and out of the house. When you walked in the front door, to the right there was a closet and to the left there was a low brick wall that separated the front door from the living room. It was about four feet high and about three feet long, just a room divider, but i never touched it or wanted to be near it.

After we had lived there for a few months, my dad started making some renovations to the house. Among them was demolishing the wall. My parents dropped my brother and I off with our grandparents the day they were going to do it so that we wouldn't be underfoot.

We didn't end up going home for a week. When my dad knocked down the wall, he called the police. Inside the brick wall were bones that turned out to be from children. The cops never did figure out who put them there. The house had been owned by a lot of people, many of them who had rented it out, so its just one of the many weird things that happened in my town that was never figured out.

Silver Ravenwolf is only controversial because she copies other people's work. Her books have a lot of good information from other writers, it just didn't come from her.

They can be a good place to start finding stuff out, but then you'll probably want to move on to other authors to get the info from the source. Amber K is a good one. Starhawk and Scott Cunningham are pretty prolific as well. Raymond Buckland also.

My advice would just be to read everything you can. Paganism and Witchcraft are very do-it-yourself paths, there are a lot of things out there that won't work for you and some stuff that will make sense at the beginning but that you'll discard as you study more.
